chunks: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Sinan, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

Verily, for Allah is a special knowledge and a general knowledge. As for the special knowledge, it is the knowledge which He did not grant access to His brought-near angels and His sent prophets. As for His general knowledge, it is His knowledge which He granted access to His brought-near angels and His sent prophets. And this has reached us from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.لَمْ يُطْلَعْ عَلَيْهِ: Did not grant access to / did not reveal

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Allah's special and general knowledge in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the distinction between Allah's exclusive, uncreated knowledge (Ilm al-Khass) and the knowledge He has delegated to His chosen servants (Ilm al-Amm). In Shia theology, this underscores the concept of divine transcendence, affirming that while prophets and angels possess profound insight, the full essence of God's knowledge remains beyond their complete comprehension, a nuance often explored in discussions of Tawhid and the nature of revelation.

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/342] al-Tawhid: Ibn al-Mutawakkil from al-Himyari from Ibn Isa from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Sinan from Ja’far b. Muhammad from his father عليهما السلام who said:

Verily there is for Allah a special knowledge and a general knowledge. As for the special knowledge then it is the knowledge which no one has seen (access to), not His angels brought-near nor His prophets who were sent. As for His general knowledge then it is His knowledge which has been seen (accessed) by His angels brought-near and His prophets who were sent. And this (last) has reached us from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه واله
